facts.raw_span: A ten-month-old Hispanic girl presented for evaluation of facial asymmetry noted since birth
the right lower lip deviates inward, whereas the rest of facial movement is symmetric
Pregnancy was uncomplicated, and the patient was born full term
Developmental milestones are appropriate for age
her face is symmetric at rest
When she smiles, the right lower lip deviates inward
frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth are symmetric on both sides
A neurodevelopmental examination is normal
Magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals is normal
echocardiography shows no cardiac anomalies
an auditory brainstem response test reveals normal hearing pathways

concepts.why: The patient's facial asymmetry noted since birth, with the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling, suggests a congenital condition.
The patient's asymmetric facial movement, with the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling, is consistent with unilateral facial paresis.
The patient's congenital condition, with the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling, suggests a congenital lower lip palsy.

concepts.preferred_label: Facial Asymmetry due to Abnormal Brain Development
concepts.why: The patient's facial asymmetry, with normal developmental milestones and a normal neurodevelopmental examination, may be related to abnormal brain development.
The patient's isolated congenital facial asymmetry, with no other associated conditions, suggests a diagnosis of isolated congenital facial asymmetry.

The patient's congenital condition, with the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling, and normal imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals, suggests a congenital cranial nerve VII palsy.
The normal imaging and laboratory results rule out other potential causes of facial asymmetry, suggesting a localized issue with the lower lip.

rationales.F02: Right lower lip deviation during smiling is a key indicator of unilateral facial paresis or congenital lower lip palsy
rationales.F06: Asymmetric facial movement during smiling is a strong indicator of congenital facial asymmetry or unilateral facial paresis

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of facial asymmetry noted since birth, with the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling or crying, are most specifically explained by Congenital Lower Lip Palsy, which directly addresses the isolated nature of the lip movement issue without implying broader neurological or developmental issues not supported by the evidence.
